project.title: VoRD: Vocabulary of Restrictive Datasets
project.description: A machine-readable vocabulary for SPARQL endpoint maintainers to publish live operational restrictions, including request rates, result sizes, evaluation time, quotas, scope, enforcement behavior, and HTTP response signals.

hero.headline: Publish the restrictions your SPARQL endpoint actually enforces.
hero.body: VoRD lets endpoint maintainers describe live restrictions as vord:Restriction resources linked from sd:Service. Query engines and users can discover request rates, result sizes, evaluation time, quotas, scopes, enforcement behavior, and HTTP signals before sending work.

overviewCards.title: For Endpoint Maintainers
overviewCards.body: Describe each important public restriction as a separate resource linked from sd:Service. Make its metric, maximum value, QUDT unit, scope, enforcement mode, and hard or advisory status explicit.

overviewCards.title: For Query Engine Developers
overviewCards.body: Discover the terms needed to plan requests, adapt workloads, and interpret endpoint responses, from vord:metric and vord:maxValue to vord:hasScope and vord:enforcement.

overviewCards.title: For Endpoint Users
overviewCards.body: Use published restrictions and examples to understand when an endpoint may reject, truncate, queue, throttle, or otherwise constrain a request or query.

customSections.title: How a VoRD Description Works
customSections.body: A service description starts with an sd:Service and links each advertised policy through vord:hasRestriction. Each restriction then states what is measured, the threshold, who or what it applies to, and how the endpoint behaves when the threshold is reached.
items: Use vord:metric, vord:maxValue, and the QUDT vord:unit to state the primary threshold.
Use vord:hasScope, vord:enforcement, and vord:hardRestriction to describe applicability and behavior.
Add vord:windowDuration and vord:burstValue for rate or quota windows where relevant.
Publish vord:retryAfterHint, vord:returnsStatusCode, and vord:httpSignalHeader when they reflect actual HTTP behavior.
